children: India’s BSE Sensex finished about 0.2% up at 74,902.6 on Thursday, halting a three-day losing run, as bargain hunters stepped in after the recent sell-off.
Volatility remained elevated, however, with the expiry of key monthly derivative contracts and the new closing auction mechanism contributing to sharp swings toward the close.
Meanwhile, investor stayed cautious amid lingering concerns over surging oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty.
Gains in banking, power and select heavyweight stocks helped offset losses in metals, pharmaceuticals and technology shares.
Power Grid was the best-performing stock, gaining 2.3%, followed by Axis Bank (1.7%), UltraTech Cement (1.4%), NTPC (1.1%), Tech Mahindra (1.1%) and Bharti Airtel (1%).
HDFC Bank, L&T and Kotak Mahindra Bank also advanced solidly.
On the losing side, HCLTech lagged with a 2.4% drop, with Tata Steel and Trent falling 1.4% and 1.1%, respectively.

title: Sensex Closes Slightly Higher
